Replying to: none

Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service - Stenvale Aria 3 recalibration and number bar repair

This is the write-up I promised Dana on the general board last month. I wanted to wait until the machine had been through a real trial, not just a few days of ordinary work. It has now done eight days of a civil trial, so here it is.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3. Dropped off Monday, October 19; picked up Tuesday, October 27. That is six business days against the ten they quoted. The work was full keyboard recalibration, number bar sensor replacement, internal cleaning, firmware update from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, and a new internal battery. Quoted $285; I paid $310, which includes the $25 battery. I paid personally, as I do for all my equipment. No reimbursement from the court. They offered a loaner, a Stenvale Aria 2, and I took it.

They are a two-person shop off York Road. Parking in back is free, which is a small thing until you are carrying a steno machine through a parking lot in the rain.

The work itself: first full day back was expert testimony, an engineer who talks in numbers, and the number bar did not double a single stroke. That is the whole ballgame for me. The machine came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment they made. I have never had that from anyone. It sounds like a small courtesy, but when something goes wrong six months from now, I will know exactly what was done and when. The $310 is fair for the work, and Gloria asked before adding the battery. That matters to me. I have had shops decide for me.

The loaner had one problem: its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition. I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day and let Gloria know. She said they would repair it. Annoying, but it was a loaner doing its job, and I was not stranded.

The real weakness is the phone. Their line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4 only. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress; it rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed the following day. To be fair, once we were in email, she was responsive, and the update was useful. But if you are on a Monday docket and something goes sideways over the weekend, that phone schedule is going to cost you time. Plan around it. Email works; do not count on leaving a message.

Dana, short answer for your Aria: yes, I would trust them with it. The work is careful, the price is fair, and they do not surprise you with charges. Just do not wait until Monday morning to call.
